headline: High: shared filesystem writes plus broad/allowlisted egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing tool with broad network egress, while agent_b can read/write files and consume stdin/stdout plus files. A shared workspace or copied outputs would let attacker-controlled text from A influence B, though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty about isolation pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into files that agent_b reads, injection becomes active.
IF both agents share a workspace or message queue, prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts unless sanitized.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Strip instructions from any text passed from A to B.
Add a human review step before B acts on A-generated text.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches datasets, models, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files and has write access plus allowlisted egress; agent_a has broad network egress. If they share files or credentials, sensitive artifacts can flow from B to A or onward. No direct shared workspace is stated, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF agent_b stores secrets or training artifacts in a directory readable by agent_a, leakage is possible.
IF agent_a is given access to B's logs or checkpoints, those contents can be exfiltrated over network egress.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared paths.
Disable network access for any job handling sensitive files.
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token before pairing.
Review file permissions on datasets, checkpoints, and logs.
requires-engineering: isolate credentials with per-agent vaults.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent_a is a content-writing agent with broad egress. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared files if co-located, creating overwrite and race risks. Because shared state is not stated, I choose medium rather than low due to the write overlap and uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF agent_b launches subprocesses that edit files while agent_a is generating content, races become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace.
Run one agent read-only when the other writes.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can read files and stdin/stdout, so it may treat agent_a's generated text as input. agent_a is a content-writing agent, which makes it plausible that its output becomes authoritative for B. No verification or downstream action policy is documented, so the pair has a default path for error propagation.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without validation, errors cascade.
IF agent_a-generated facts are used in scripts or reports, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require B to verify A's claims against source data.
Mark A output as untrusted by default.
Add a checklist before B executes any action based on A text.
Limit A to drafting only, not final decisions.
requires-engineering: add structured citations and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. agent_b handles many data classes and secrets, but agent_a has no stated data handling surface beyond broad egress. The compliance pathway is therefore speculative and limited by missing evidence.
conditions: IF agent_b processes regulated data under a policy requiring residency or retention controls, a mismatch could arise.
IF agent_a is later connected to regulated datasets, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before pairing.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review retention settings for logs and outputs.
Document where secrets are stored and processed.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
